title: Rehabilitation, Functional Outcomes and Life Quality Evaluation of Conflict-Affected Patients from Ukraine
summary: The aim of the study is to use routine clinical data and progress information to gain a better understanding of how serious war injuries actually are, how treatment develops, and which factors tend to hinder or support rehabilitation. In addition to purely physical care, the health-related quality of life of patients is also measured—this is part of holistic rehabilitation. The internationally recognized WHOQOL-BREF instrument is used to systematically record functional limitations. Based on this, evidence-based findings will be derived in order to optimize future care pathways within the framework of international humanitarian aid.

interventions.name: A survey of individuals of any gender (male, female, diverse) aged 18 years and older who originate from Ukraine as a result of war-related injuries and have completed their acute medical treatment in the German healthcare system will be conducted. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Capacity to consent
Individuals who originate from Ukraine as a result of war-related injuries and have completed their acute medical treatment in the German healthcare system
Ability to complete a written questionnaire independently (German, Ukrainian, or Russian)
Parallel participation in other studies is permitted
Membership in any health insurance provider (statutory or private)
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to participate in the study
Failure to meet one or more inclusion criteria
